transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, what brings me in is that... most nights, once my wife goes to bed, I end up in the kitchen. And I just eat way past what a normal plate would be. 

Like, I'll eat fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls... really just whatever event leftovers are in there. I'll just keep going until a whole tray is empty, or like, half the fridge is just gone.
How long has this been happening? When did you first notice yourself eating this way at night?

It's been going on for a while now. I guess it started right around the time the foreclosure process began on our house. So, that would make it about a year and two months now that I've been doing this.
During these episodes when you're eating in the kitchen at night, do you feel like you have control over how much you're eating, or does it feel like you can't stop even if you wanted to?

I don't feel like I have any control at all. It's... well, once I take that very first bite, it really feels like the decision has already been made for me. I'll literally be standing there in the kitchen telling myself, "George, stop now," but my hands just keep going. They just keep fixing another plate or opening up another container from the fridge. I just can't stop it once I start.
After these eating episodes at night, do you do anything to try to compensate or make up for what you've eaten—like making yourself vomit, exercising excessively, or fasting the next day?

No, I don't do any of that. I just... I go to sleep feeling awful, but I don't throw up or skip meals the next day or anything. I just wake up and eat normally, or try to, anyway. I definitely don't exercise like crazy either.
Besides these eating episodes at night, how has your mood been over this past year or so? Have you been feeling sad, empty, or like things just don't feel enjoyable anymore?

I don't think so. I mean, I'm stressed about the house and everything, but I wouldn't say I feel sad or empty. I still enjoy the things I usually like to do, when I have the time. It's really just the stress of the situation, not like a deep sadness or anything like that.
When you get the urge to go to the kitchen at night and start eating, does it feel like there's a buildup of tension or pressure inside you that gets relieved once you start eating?

No, I wouldn't really describe it like that. I don't feel a buildup of tension or pressure before I go in there. It's just... I get the urge to eat, and then I'm doing it. And it definitely doesn't feel like a relief once I start. If anything, I just feel worse about myself while it's happening.

These nighttime eating episodes—how much have they affected your life? For example, have they impacted your work, your relationships with your wife or others, or how you feel about yourself day-to-day?

It’s definitely affecting my day-to-day life. I mean, I'm not working right now, but I used to be pretty involved in our community planning meetings and helping out with local events. Lately, I've just... I've completely pulled back from all of that. 

I feel embarrassed, mostly, and just really drained from the whole thing. I guess I'm afraid people will look at me and notice that I’m not holding things together the way I used to. So yeah, it definitely takes a toll on how I feel about myself around other people.
On average, how many nights per week would you say you're going to the kitchen and having these uncontrolled eating episodes?

Well, for months now, I honestly can't think of a single week where it didn't happen at least once. But usually... most weeks, it's been several nights. I just wait until my wife goes to bed, and then it happens. So, yeah, it's pretty frequent.
Have you noticed changes in your weight or how your body looks since these eating episodes started about a year ago?

Honestly, I haven't really noticed. I don't step on the scale or anything, and... I guess I just try not to look too closely in the mirror these days. So I can't really say if my weight has changed or not.

You mentioned you don't make yourself vomit or fast the next day. But I want to be thorough—have you ever used laxatives, diuretics, or any other methods to try to get rid of what you've eaten or prevent weight gain?
No, I don't do anything like that. I don't use laxatives or water pills or anything. I just... I eat, and then I go to bed. I don't try to get rid of it or make up for it the next day.
When you think about these nighttime eating episodes and how they've been affecting you, would you say they cause you significant distress or emotional pain?

Yeah, they really do. Afterward... I just feel sick with myself. It's like, everybody sees me as this organized, strong man, but then I'm just sitting there completely ashamed and guilty. I just feel disgusted that I let it happen again.
